scope: Japan-origin 100 g sealed manufactured steamed/dried pure sencha, paid personal postal purchase; ordinary customs/post declarations and arrival inspection allowed, no separate agency application/approval, origin certificate or registration.
interpretation: This bounded research pass is complete; no country in this batch is newly verified. A narrower missing question is not a completed country.

records.finding: The saved ACONOQ programme guide expressly exempts e-commerce postal parcels and low-value imports from PCEC. This is a genuine scope exception, so conformity cannot justify exclusion.
records.gap: No newly located operative plant-product definition/commodity condition settles manufactured tea and personal post. WTO generic plant-product authorization is insufficient.

records.finding: Saved 2026 official report confirms Proclamation156/2006 remains applicable. Its manufactured-product scope depends on pest risk; later food-policy work is still drafting.
records.gap: No new operative national classification or personal-food import rule; inspection and certificates issued at arrival alone do not breach the constraint.

records.finding: The signed Order A/2024/920/MCIPME/CAB/SGG of 10 June 2024 is now recovered from the official BNIQ library. Article 2 includes imports for final-consumer use; Article 3 limits its stated scope to merchandise transported in containers, trucks and other international rolling transport. Article 4 begins with an exemption statement, then says samples, gifts, objects not intended for sale and other noncommercial articles may be exempt. Article 5 excludes Article 4 goods from its separate electronic inspection declaration. For covered imports Article 6 requires foreign quality or quality-assurance certificates and, for plants and their products, origin official quarantine certificates. These are independent origin-document duties, unlike the positive arrival inspection report issued under Articles 10–12. The order does not expressly settle its Article 3 transport scope or Article 4 exception for a paid private air-post tea parcel. Its own plant-product provision also does not define manufactured tea. The BNIQ manual describes company registration with RCCM and NIF, not a private-post procedure.
records.gap: The new signed 2024 BNIQ order establishes a special declaration/origin-document route for covered goods, but Article 3 transport scope and the Article 4 non-sale/noncommercial exception leave applicability to this paid private postal order unresolved. Independent plant-law pest-risk classification remains missing. Do not infer a private certificate duty from the company-only platform manual, or infer a plant-health waiver from an inspection exception.

records.finding: Existing NPPO/UPU and border material does not supply the missing operative finished-tea rule.
records.gap: A current national food or plant-product import provision reaching this personal postal commodity remains unavailable. No unsupported waiver or blanket duty inferred.

records.finding: Decree-Law4/99 covers unprocessed or simply prepared plant products; Decree62-E/1992 delegates food-import documentary conditions and certification to implementing regulation.
records.gap: No new operative implementing condition or processing category for steamed/dried tea. Enabling powers alone cannot establish private certificate duty.

records.finding: Food Law17-005/AU expressly includes personal food, but the examined certificate clauses concern animal goods/import businesses. Foreign-trade Law21-013/AU delegates product lists and technical-control methods.
records.gap: No adopted implementing list/method settling manufactured tea; the blank-number/date2022 drafts remain excluded as enactment evidence.

records.finding: Enacted DM98/2023 Article4 excludes postal parcels from PAC without a separate application. This excludes a conformity-based refusal.
records.gap: Decree5/2009 manufactured-product pest-risk scope is not resolved by the unrelated PAC waiver, propagation entries, or empty public commodity-search results.

records.finding: The actual1976 Notice includes dried materials but has a potentially relevant cooked-material exception and ambiguous container qualifier. The available2017 food Bill is not the authenticated final2018 Act referenced in subsequent enacted law.
records.gap: Whether steaming satisfies the Notice exception, and the final private-import food duty, remain open. No unsupported correction of item64 or extension of business/import-for-sale provisions.

records.finding: The2011 fee schedule expressly includes tea, but an inspection fee is not a special-document requirement. Actual2020 prior declaration order requires annual company/operator data.
records.gap: No private postal implementation or exemption recovered; company-focused annual approval cannot be applied automatically to the private recipient.

records.finding: Regulation7 offers destination inspection without a pre-export CoC; Regulation8 accepts customs declarations and makes an exemption letter conditional. Therefore the low-value exemption letter alone is not a sound exclusion while that alternate route remains.
records.gap: Private-post operation of the destination-inspection path and independent manufactured-tea pest-risk classification remain unresolved. No repeat of the previously exhausted official PDF403 retrieval.
